topStory.headline: Opinion: Colleges Face Choice to Shape A.I. Impact or Be Redefined By It
topStory.summary:
A guest commentary in the Columbia Missourian argues that higher education institutions must decide whether to actively integrate A.I. into their learning ecosystems or be passively reshaped by the technology. The opinion piece highlights a tension between embracing A.I. as a tool for enhancing education versus the risk of institutions being transformed by technological change without strategic direction.

The article questions whether universities are taking intentional steps to ensure A.I. serves their educational missions or whether they risk having those missions dictated by technological advancement. The commentary frames A.I. integration as a strategic choice requiring institutional engagement rather than passive acceptance.

stories.headline: Florida International University Hosts Presidential Summit on Higher Education Disruption
stories.summary: At a recent summit hosted by Florida International University, leaders from various sectors discussed how higher education must adapt amid rapid technological change. According to FIU News, participants emphasized the need for universities to collaborate with industry to ensure students are equipped with skills to navigate an A.I.-driven job market.

stories.headline: South Korean University Integrates A.I. Across Campus Operations
stories.summary: Chungnam National University in South Korea is integrating A.I. across campus life, from chatbots to academic support systems. According to Evrimagaci.org, the university is embedding technology into its operations as part of a comprehensive A.I. adoption strategy.

stories.headline: N.C. A&T Faculty Selected for CAA A.I. Technologies Champion Network
stories.summary: Faculty members from North Carolina A&T have been selected for the CAA's A.I. Technologies Champion Network inaugural award. According to Yes Weekly, the recognition highlights the role of individual educators in leading A.I. integration efforts within institutions.

stories.headline: Survey: Half of U.S. Academics Say Universities Unprepared for A.I.
stories.summary: Half of U.S. academics report that universities are unprepared for A.I. despite its widespread use, according to VarIndia. The survey results highlight a gap between A.I. adoption levels and institutional readiness to manage and guide that adoption.

stories.headline: Pearson Data Links A.I. Study Tools to Increased Active Reading
stories.summary: Pearson data links A.I. study tools to a surge in active reading among college students, according to EdTech Innovation Hub. The findings suggest technology-enhanced learning may boost engagement with course materials.

stories.headline: Community Colleges Emphasize Strategy Before Technology in A.I. Adoption
stories.summary: Community colleges are finding that successful A.I. adoption requires putting strategy before technology, according to Community College Daily. The approach focuses on educational goals rather than pursuing the latest tools without clear purpose.
